preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.splitlines()[0]) and n >= 1 and n <= 10**5
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the number of registration requests.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) > 0 and line.islower() and line.isalpha() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:n+1])
preconditions.description: Each of the next n lines is a non-empty string of lowercase Latin letters (length ≤ 32).

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines() == [process_request(requests[i], database_up_to_i) for i in range(n)]
postconditions.description: For each request in the input (stored in `requests`), the output line is the system's response: 'OK' if the name is not in the database at the time of the request, or the smallest available name of the form `request + str(i)` (where `i` starts at 1) if the name is already taken. The `database_up_to_i` is the set of all previously registered names (including prompts) up to and including the i-th request.

postconditions.expression: all(response == 'OK' or (response.startswith(request) and response[len(request):].isdigit()) for request, response in zip(requests, stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: Every response is either 'OK' or a valid prompt formed by appending a positive integer to the original request name.

postconditions.expression: all(response != 'OK' or response not in database_up_to_i for request, response, database_up_to_i in zip(requests, stdout.splitlines(), [set(requests[:i]) for i in range(1, n+1)]))
postconditions.description: If the response is 'OK', the requested name is not in the database at the time of the request. If the response is a prompt, it is the smallest available name of the form `request + str(i)` not already in the database.
